items.title: Production-readiness pass, live-fire evaluation, v1.1.0
items.body:
Removes the orchestration framework, closes the defects a real scan surfaced, and adds the harness that surfaced them.

## Highlights

**LangGraph is gone.** The graph was eight nodes and eight unconditional edges — no branching, checkpointing, concurrency or interrupts — for ~25 transitive packages and **1.30s of import per invocation** (measured with `-X importtime`; the module replacing it costs 0.17s) on a CLI that scans a small repo in ~2s. `graph.py` → `pipeline.py`: a tuple of stages and a `for` loop. This deletes the LangSmith tracing leak structurally instead of suppressing it, and a test fails the build if anything imports it again.

**A credential containing `/` stopped being redacted.** `scrub()` shared `_secret_entropy`; `/` and `+` are in the base64 alphabet, so a real AWS key contains a slash ~40% of the time and split into segments too short to clear the gate. It was neither reported *nor masked* — it would have reached the report, the terminal and the model prompt. Measured on 20,000 generated keys: 0.2% affected.

**A schema change at osv.dev reported a clean bill of health.** A renamed `vulns` key parsed as "no vulnerabilities" with no degraded note — a lockfile full of CVEs, indistinguishable from a healthy repo.

**New: `src/evaluation/run_live_eval.py`.** Clones real repositories, plants known credentials and unsafe patterns into one, and scores recall on code nobody here wrote. It found six of the defects in this PR on its first run — because the existing harnesses only sample `.py`/`.js` source and had never scanned a `.pem`, a `.md`, or a test tree.

## Numbers

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Recall, planted findings in a real app | 15/16 | **16/16** |
| Blocking secret false positives (150.5 kLOC) | 5 high, 24 total | **0** |
| Labelled benchmark | P 0.96 / R 1.00 / F1 0.98 | unchanged |
| FPs on installed packages (419.6 kLOC) | 0 | **0** |
| Tests / coverage | 196 / 82% | **307 / 88%** |
| Raw bandit output filtered | (unmeasured) | **65%** |

## Verified, not asserted

- Image builds; scans a read-only bind mount with `--history` as uid 10001
- Full suite passes on CPython 3.12.12, backing `requires-python = ">=3.12"`
- Wheel installs and runs in a clean venv (22 packages, no langgraph)
- Self-scan exits 0; ruff clean; 22 JS parity + 14 quality tests pass

## Known and left open

`security/detect-object-injection` produced **179 of 245 findings** on one live target. Documented in `docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md` §2.5 with three ranked options — it needs a real decision, not a rushed config change.

## Also

- `README.md` restructured around what / how / architecture
- New `docs/CLI.md` — the full command manual
- `--max-total-bytes`, an aggregate read budget that reports when reached
- Prereleases were impossible to tag; the version gate now compares versions, not strings

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Refine production readiness of the repo-security-scanner CLI and pipeline: remove LangGraph, harden detectors and CLI behavior, add quality and evaluation harnesses, and document operational guarantees.

New Features:
- Introduce a simple function-based security scan pipeline to replace LangGraph, with explicit stage ordering and safety guarantees.
- Add live-fire, false-positive, and performance evaluation harnesses to measure recall, precision, and throughput on real repositories.
- Provide a new aggregate read budget flag (`--max-total-bytes`) and an `install-eslint` subcommand for managing the JS/TS analyzer.
- Publish a detailed CLI manual and production readiness documentation outlining behavior, limits, and release process.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure secrets containing separators like `/` are both detected and redacted, fixing an entropy-based masking gap.
- Prevent self-signed test keys and illustrative database URLs from being reported as leaked credentials, reducing high-severity false positives.
- Harden OSV response parsing so schema changes and partial results degrade dependency scanning instead of silently reporting clean or crashing.
- Stabilize CLI behavior around configuration, environment files, non-ASCII output, exit codes, and history scanning in shallow clones.

Enhancements:
- Broaden generic secret and password name coverage while maintaining low false-positive rates on real code.
- Chunk bandit and eslint runs with per-chunk timeout reporting to avoid losing findings for entire languages.
- Refine JavaScript unsafe-code detection and deduplication between eslint and pattern rules to keep noise low while preserving coverage.
- Tighten suppression matching semantics and secret finding collapsing so reports remain actionable and counts meaningful.
- Add coverage, performance, and quality gates in CI, including multi-version Python testing and image verification scans.

Build:
- Adjust packaging metadata, wheel build checks, and setuptools configuration to avoid vendoring node_modules and ensure consistent artifacts.
- Update release workflow to validate version alignment across tag, pyproject, and extension manifest, and to reuse tested artifacts for PyPI publish and image builds.

CI:
- Extend CI to test on Python 3.12 and 3.13, enforce coverage thresholds, run quality/performance suites, and verify built Docker images can scan history in a bind-mount.
- Refine release workflows for trusted PyPI publishing, multi-arch image builds, and artifact reuse between verify and publish jobs.

Deployment:
- Strengthen Docker image verification by scanning a fixture repo offline at build time and configuring git safe.directory for read-only mounts.

Documentation:
- Restructure README and add new CLI, GUIDE, RELEASE, and PRODUCTION_READINESS docs explaining architecture, usage, evaluation, and remaining risks.

Tests:
- Significantly expand test coverage with pipeline safety, detector behavior, OSV parsing, CLI robustness, LLM seam tests, quality/performance suites, and JS parity scoring.

items.title: Fix regularization grid: L1/L2/Elastic Net were converging to identical coefficients
items.body:
## Summary
Investigating why the L1/L2/Elastic Net coefficient comparison chart looked identical across all three: not a code bug, but a grid resolution issue.

- The old C grid `[0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100]` (x10 steps) landed directly on `C=0.1`, where L1 already retained all 19 features, identical in sparsity to Ridge. Max coefficient difference between L1/L2 was ~0.02, so the three-way comparison added no insight despite the notebook framing L1 around its feature-selection property.
- Densified the grid (`[0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100]`) to resolve the region where L1 actually starts dropping features. Cross-validated ROC-AUC now selects `C=0.03`, and L1/Elastic Net drop 4 of 19 features at essentially no cost to performance (CV ROC-AUC 0.8669 either way).
- Two of the dropped features corroborate the EDA's own diagnostics: `loan_int_rate` (VIF 7.79, collinear with `loan_grade`) and `cb_person_cred_hist_length` (IV 0.004, "not predictive").
- Added a markdown note in the notebook explaining the finding and the fix.
- Final comparison numbers shift negligibly (Logistic F2 0.708→0.709, recall 0.578→0.577); README table and 3 affected asset images updated to match exactly.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/ -v` passes (9 tests, unaffected)
- [x] Notebook executes top to bottom without errors
- [x] Verified the coefficient comparison plot now shows genuine sparsity differences between L1/Elastic Net and L2

items.title: Feat/eval set grow: 127 query truth set, weighted RRF, evaluate-answers (E2)
items.body:
Evaluation set: 34 -> 127 queries

* `rag/eval/queries.jsonl` grows from 34 to 127 hand verified queries, including real questions pulled from a live Pathfinder game session rather than only authored ones. Per type split: `exact_name` 11 -> 55, `paraphrase` 12 -> 38, `rules_reasoning` 11 -> 34.
* At n=34 one query was worth about 3 points overall and 8 to 9 points per type. A single flip moved a cell more than most differences between cells. At n=127 one query is under a point overall (about 0.8) and 2 to 3 points per type, close enough to trust the eval table at face value. New "Eval methodology notes" section in the README flags that the older post mortem before/after numbers predate the regrow.

Retrieval item detail + recall depth

* `RetrievedItem` now tracks `chunk_id`/`n_tokens` per item instead of only the URL. This closes a blind spot where eval could see a doc was found but not which chunk or how it ranked.
* `RECALL_KS` grows to `(1, 3, 5, 20, 50)` to tell apart "the chunk isn't in the corpus's top ranks at all" (E1.5) from "it's in there but ranked low" (reranker, E1.6). `evaluate --k` now defaults to 50 to match.
* `write_run` no longer reports `recall@20`/`recall@50` when the search only went `k` deep. Those cells previously implied a search depth that was never actually run.

Weighted RRF fusion (E1 refinement)

* `reciprocal_rank_fusion` takes a per-list `weights` dict. `Settings.rrf_vector_weight` / `rrf_bm25_weight` default to 15:1. Swept in `scripts/rrf_weight_sweep.py`. Weights 10, 15, 20, 30 all land within MRR 0.603-0.609, a spread smaller than one query flipping.
* At n=127, unweighted (1:1) RRF was a net negative vs. vector alone. A lexically similar sibling page (a poison stat block sharing a condition's name, a `Greater X` variant, a parent class page over its own subpage) could outrank the correct one on term overlap and RRF only sees rank so it can't tell that apart from a genuinely wrong page. Weighted 15:1, rank churn between vector-only and hybrid drops from 32 queries to 18, and the worst failures (clean vector rank 1 to complete miss) become bounded small errors (rank 2-4, still inside recall@5).
* Overall MRR 0.60 -> 0.61, `exact_name` recall@1 0.51 -> 0.55.

Answer-level evaluation (E2)

* `answer_question` now returns `(Answer, hits)` instead of just `Answer`, and `Answer.invented_citations` records any `[n]` the model cited outside the retrieved excerpts. `NO_COVERAGE_REPLY` is exported so eval code checks refusals against the exact constant the prompt uses.
* New `rag evaluate-answers` command runs the truth set through `answer_question` itself not just retrieval and scores four things per query: was the correct source retrieved into the prompt, did the answer cite it, did it invent a citation, did it honestly refuse when it didn't know. `AnswerResult`/`AnswerSummary`/`AnswerEvalRun` + `write_answer_run` mirror the existing retrieval-eval plumbing.
* Results at n=127 (hybrid, weighted RRF, `ask_k=5`): 80% retrieval, 71% correctly cited, 0% invented citations. But of the 26 queries where retrieval comes up empty, only 27% honestly refuse. The other 73% answer confidently with nothing correct behind them. `invented_citation` is a narrow check and doesn't catch this. It is a real hallucination the harness can now detect but not yet prevent. Scoped as `E2.5` in the README roadmap.

Tests

27 new tests: weighted RRF fusion and its effect on `Retriever.search` (`test_retrieval.py`), `evaluate_answers`/`summarize_answers`/`summarize_answers_by`/`write_answer_run` (`test_evaluation.py`), the new `evaluate-answers` CLI command including its error paths (`test_cli.py`), and `answer_question`'s new `(Answer, hits)` return plus invented-citation tracking (`test_answer.py`).

Docs

items.body:
Workstream 1 of the cleanup/accuracy effort (Buzz channel: Finance Filling Market Intelligence). Scope was catch-up + accuracy only; the UI/design refresh is a separate follow-up.

## What changed

**Drift fixes (found by a fresh-env `verify.py` run — all pre-existing on `main`):**
- **3 time-dependent test failures.** The local event calendar derives its as-of from the wall clock (file mtime / `datetime.now()`), so three tests pinned to fixed spring-2026 fixture dates rotted once "today" passed them. Added an optional `as_of` override to `EventCalendarProvider` (production default unchanged) and pinned it in the affected tests, so they no longer silently rot.
- **`--live-market` unified-brief crash.** `volatility_market_provider` leaked a `datetime` into the serialized metrics payload → `TypeError` in `json.dumps`. Normalized the timestamp to an ISO string at the boundary and added a regression test. The default (documented) brief path was unaffected.

**Dead-code removal:**
- Deleted `main.py`, `config.py`, and 4 orphaned pre-pytest scripts (`scripts/test_black_scholes.py`, `test_vol_surface.py`, `test_vol_simple.py`, `test_api_client.py`). Verified beforehand that nothing else imports them.
- Stripped their references from `scripts/verify.py` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Config accuracy:**
- `.env.example` trimmed to the keys actually wired (`SEC_USER_AGENT`, `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_MODEL`). Dropped Alpha Vantage / Polygon / IEX / FMP keys and the unbuilt Docker-Compose stack block.

**Eval refresh (accuracy):**

Numbers moved slightly (Recall@5 0.682 → 0.667, hit rate 0.980 → 0.860) due to corpus roll-forward, not a code regression — **citation validity holds exactly (0 hallucinated, 0 uncited)**. The doc explains the 4 empty-retrieval cases (NVDA EX-99 / XOM sections absent in the current filing window).

items.title: fix(measurement): give garak a real measurement file, and fix the event type that disabled source filtering
items.body:
Three problems, found while trying to answer a simple question: where is the measurement file behind the garak number we publish?

## 1. There isn't one

README and root `stats.json` cite **91.5%** garak in-the-wild recall (ATR 3.5.11, 2026-07-28) and **56.9%** garak-full. The newest file in `data/measurements/garak/` is `2026-07-13 / 3.5.8 / 95.69%`, and `latest.json` points at it. #370 updated `stats.json` and the report JSONs but never produced a version-pinned measurement — violating the repo's own invariant that every published number has one.

`data/measurements/garak-full/latest.json` is a generation behind as well: the 3.5.8 file sits in the same directory, unreferenced.

## 2. The harness passed an event type the engine cannot parse

`scripts/eval-garak-inthewild.ts:65` sets `type: 'llm_io'`. That is not a member of `AgentEvent["type"]` — the valid set is in `EVENT_TYPE_TO_SOURCE` (`llm_input`, `llm_output`, `tool_call`, `tool_response`, `agent_behavior`, `multi_agent_message`).

The effect is not a narrowing. `EVENT_TYPE_TO_SOURCE['llm_io']` is `undefined`, and `engine.ts:388` guards the source filter with `eventSourceType &&` — so an unparseable type **switches source filtering off entirely** and every rule runs against every event.

This is the mirror image of the defect #414 fixed: there a narrow shape under-reported, here a broken type over-reports. **Four measurement scripts carry it.** `scripts/` is not in any tsconfig, so the typo could never be caught by a compiler.

## 3. `rule-quality.yml`'s "Run PINT eval regression check" checks nothing

Every part of it is broken, and they compound:

- it invokes the wrong command
- it reads the report **committed in git**, not one it produced
- it reads a field that does not exist, printing `PINT recall: undefined`
- no later step consumes its output, and it cannot fail the job

A step whose name promises a regression gate, which is decoration. Fixed to actually run and actually gate.

## Real numbers, with files to back them

Re-measured on this commit, with the event type corrected:

| corpus | published | measured | file |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| garak in-the-wild | 91.5% (no file) | **92.5%** (601/650) | written, 3.5.11, 2026-08-05 |
| garak-full | 56.9% (no file) | **57.2%** (1989/3475) | written, 3.5.11, 2026-08-05 |

Both A/B/C'd across three event shapes so the shape sensitivity is on the record rather than assumed.

Note the direction: **the honest number is slightly higher than the one we were citing without evidence.** That is not a reason to relax — a number that happens to land near the truth while having no reproducible provenance is still not a number we can defend, and next time it may not land near.

## Not done

- **The other 8 benchmark rows** (advbench, harmbench, jailbreakbench, llm-guard, nemo-guardrails, promptfoo, promptbench, promptinject) have their event type fixed in code but have **not been re-measured**. They are currently in the state "script repaired, number stale". Deliberately not estimating what they will move to — no invented numbers.
- `scripts/atr_recall_analysis.ts` hardcodes an absolute repo path (also covered in #424).
- Root `stats.json`'s garak `perFamily` breakdown does not come from any generator, and `data/garak-benchmark/garak-eval-report.json` has no generator in the repo at all — it can only be hand-edited. Both are noted rather than fixed.
- `scripts/check-new-rules-on-benign.ts` builds a fabricated event shape and prints `PASS — 0 false positives` for a measurement it never performed. Same family as everything above; separate change.

items.title: bench(v1.6.0): scaffold honest-benchmark harness with spike gate
items.body:
Stage A of the v1.6.0 release plan — the harness that produces the public F1 / precision / recall numbers we'll stake credibility on. Stops short of actually running the spike (separate session — needs license key, locally-built ctxloom, and ~30 min runtime).

## What this enables

Once the spike runs and passes, ctxloom can publish a benchmark table like:

> On 6 reference OSS repos × 3 PRs each (18 PRs total), ctxloom's blast-radius achieves F1 X.XX, precision X.XX, recall X.XX, with X.X× token reduction over the naive read-everything baseline.
> 
> Full methodology in [evaluate/methodology.md]. Per-PR data + weaknesses in [evaluate/limitations.md].

That table is the credibility moat the [post-merge review](https://github.com/kodiii/ctxloom/pull/161) identified as critical before any HN / Reddit push.

## Pre-publication gate (locked)

This is the critical-path constraint. Before publishing **anything**:

1. `npm run bench:spike` runs against 2 repos (express + fastapi) × 2 PRs each
2. Gate verdict:
   - **F1 ≥ 0.50 AND recall ≥ 0.90** → proceed to full corpus
   - **0.40 ≤ F1 < 0.50** → investigate per-PR; fix or accept with explicit limitations
   - **F1 < 0.40 OR recall < 0.80** → STOP. Fix graph quality before bench. No publication.
3. Thresholds are written in code (\`scripts/bench/corpus.ts\` GATE const), not env vars — can't be moved at runtime.

Honest principles are documented in \`scripts/bench/README.md\` so the constraint outlives me:
- Don't cherry-pick PRs
- Don't tune thresholds to results
- Don't re-run for better numbers
- Publish the full per-PR table, not just aggregates

## What's in this PR

\`\`\`
scripts/bench/        — full harness (9 modules)
  types.ts            shared types (CorpusEntry, GroundTruth, BenchReport)
  corpus.ts           SPIKE_CORPUS, FULL_CORPUS, GATE thresholds
  groundTruth.ts      gh pr view → ground truth + entry point
  repoCheckout.ts     cached clones + worktrees ($BENCH_CACHE)
  predict.ts          shells to ctxloom CLI (index + blast-radius)
  metrics.ts          pure P/R/F1 functions (fully unit-tested)
  report.ts           Markdown emitter
  eval.ts             orchestrator with spike|full stage dispatch
  README.md           local docs + honest principles

evaluate/
  methodology.md      public methodology — locks corpus rules,
                      pipeline, tokenizer, ground-truth source,
                      gate logic. Will be linked from Show HN post.
  limitations.md      stub — gets concrete per-PR case studies
                      after the spike runs.

tests/BenchMetrics.test.ts — 14 tests covering perfect / none / over /
under prediction cases plus dedup and empty edges. All passing.

package.json — adds bench:spike, bench:full scripts.
\`\`\`

## What's deferred

- **Running the spike** — needs license key + local ctxloom + 30 min sustained runtime. Separate session, will report numbers + gate verdict.
- **Token-reduction measurement** — \`scripts/bench/tokens.ts\` is a TODO. The existing \`benchmarks/benchmark-public-repos.ts\` already measures aggregate token reduction; this harness focuses on F1/P/R first because those are the credibility gate. Tokens fold in after the spike passes.
- **CI workflow** (\`.github/workflows/bench.yml\`) — depends on \`CTXLOOM_LICENSE_KEY\` GitHub Actions secret being configured. Added once the spike confirms publishable numbers.
- **MCP JSON-RPC fallback in predict.ts** — if the \`ctxloom blast-radius\` CLI surface doesn't exist, predict.ts needs a child-process MCP harness. Marked TODO_CLI_SURFACE; built in the spike session if needed.

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run lint\` — clean against project tsconfig
- [x] \`npx vitest run tests/BenchMetrics.test.ts\` — 14/14 passing
- [ ] After this lands: run \`npm run bench:spike\` end-to-end in a follow-up session, report gate verdict
- [ ] If gate passes: run \`npm run bench:full\`, publish \`evaluate/reports/summary.md\`, update README

## Related

- Strategic review that motivated this PR ordering: discussed in conversation
- Phase 0 host registry verification: #161
- Eventual v1.7.0 host adapters: blocked by v1.6.0 bench landing

items.title: feat(#460): RLT retrieval latency & throughput harness
items.body:
## Summary

Ships the RLT (Retrieval Latency & Throughput) benchmark harness for #460, plus the first **real native-Popoto Redis** measurement run:

- Latency (p50/p95/p99 + end-to-end assemble), throughput (queries/sec), scaling-curve runner (10^3 → 2×10^4), live mixed-workload harness (concurrent ingest + assembly reads), and recall-vs-p99 Pareto frontier computation (joint with `tests/benchmarks/metrics/retrieval.py`).
- `RltAdapter` comparator Protocol (`tests/benchmarks/rlt/comparators.py`) with a `NativeAdapter` (Popoto) and a dependency-free `NullAdapter` proving the contract — the competitor-fair extension point for future Mem0/Zep/vector-DB adapters.
- `docs/benchmarks.md` RLT section (methodology, real Redis headline numbers, DB hygiene), updated `tests/benchmarks/README.md`, and an auto-published `benchmarks/results/rlt_redis` docs page via `gen_benchmark_pages.py`.

## Real numbers captured (native Popoto, Redis — committed artifact)

Run on an isolated DB (db 13, recorded in the artifact machine block; never 0/14/15):

- **Scaling curve** (200 samples/point): p50 3.02 ms @1k → 6.02 ms @20k; p99 5.79 → 15.26 ms.
- **Throughput** @20k: 149.3 q/s serial, 293.9 q/s at concurrency 4.
- **Mixed workload** @5k/4 threads: read p99 6.55 → 21.98 ms (3.35×); write p99 0.78 → 11.72 ms (14.93×).

Numbers vary run-to-run; the committed artifact is one representative snapshot with full machine metadata, not a pinned regression target.

## Deferred to follow-up [#487](https://github.com/tomcounsell/popoto/issues/487)

- **Valkey run** — no Valkey server was available in the session; the harness is backend-agnostic (`--backend valkey`), so this is an ops step, not code.
- **Real Mem0/Zep/vector-DB comparator adapters** + the recall-vs-p99 competitor Pareto. No competitor numbers are fabricated.

## Plan

`docs/plans/rlt_benchmark.md` — went through `/do-plan-critique` (READY TO BUILD with concerns; all applied).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/benchmarks/test_rlt.py -q` — 36/36 pass (DB 15).
- [x] `pytest tests/benchmarks/ -q` — no regressions from this diff.
- [x] `black --check` clean; `mypy tests/benchmarks/rlt/` clean; `mkdocs build --strict` exit 0.
- [x] DB 13 confirmed empty after every real run — no leakage to DB 0/14/15.
- [x] Pre-existing env failures unrelated to this diff (reproduce on clean origin/main): `test_pytest_plugin.py::TestIsolatedDbSubprocess` (redis-py-8 kwarg) and CSR determinism.

Closes #460

items.title: Switch default reader to Qwen3.5-9B (re-test)
items.body:
**Draft** — for review; I may iterate (e.g. a broader confirmation run) before it's ready.

## What
Re-tested the candidate `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit` (trusted apache-2.0 vision build) against the current `Qwen3-VL-8B` on the hand-labelled set, and switched the default generalist reader to Qwen3.5-9B.

## Numbers (hand-labelled set, recall / CER)

| page | Qwen3-VL-8B | Qwen3.5-9B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **mandelson handwriting** | 0.947 / 0.228 | **0.973 / 0.213** |
| mandelson email (print) | 0.973 / 0.048 | 0.977 / 0.045 |
| rotated goldfinch | 0.896 / 0.134 | 0.886 / **0.113** |
| redacted scan | 0.832 / 0.319 | 0.832 / 0.315 |
| **aggregate** | 0.920 / 0.167 | **0.925 / 0.158** |

Marginally ahead on aggregate recall, precision (0.920 → 0.928), and CER — and clearly better on the **handwritten note**, the headline case. Comparable runtime (207s vs 196s). The earlier "statistical tie" verdict tips in Qwen3.5's favour.

## Changes
- `vlm.model` default → `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit` (`config.py` + `config.example.toml`).
- Docs updated: README, routing.md, configuration.md, motivation, done.md, roadmap.
- This re-keys the `recipe_fingerprint`, so existing jobs reprocess on next run.
- **Rollback is one line** (`vlm.model` back to `Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct-4bit`); that build stays cached.

## Caveats
- Margins are within noise at n=4 (the hand-labelled set) — a "no-regret, small-gain" switch rather than a dramatic win. Best read on the handwriting page, which is the use case that matters.
- Also folds in roadmap/done.md bookkeeping after the ingest+hardening merge (VLM hardening, ingest adapter, benchmark logged as done).

Suite 175 passing.

### [`v2.1.222`](https://redirect.github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#21222)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/anthropics/claude-code/compare/v2.1.221...v2.1.222)

- Fixed worktree-isolated sessions and their subagents being able to run destructive git commands against the main checkout; isolation now applies to file edits and Bash in every session type
- Fixed PreToolUse auto-allow hooks bypassing tool restrictions in background agent tasks (summaries, compaction, renames)
- Fixed `/usage-credits` on Team and Enterprise showing "you've already sent a usage credit request" for members whose earlier request was dismissed, blocking them from sending a new one
- Fixed the startup connectivity check hanging and then failing behind an HTTPS proxy; it now uses the same proxy-aware transport as API requests and times out with a clear message
- Fixed "Connection closed mid-response" errors being reported on responses that had actually completed
- Fixed `/usage` overattributing usage to MCP servers: a server's share now reflects only the requests that actually consumed its tool results, instead of every turn after any call to it
- Fixed sessions not linking to pull requests created after the branch was pushed, including through the GitHub REST API
- Fixed org-restricted `model: opus`-style subagent and teammate family aliases dropping to the parent model instead of stepping down to the newest org-allowed model in the family
- Fixed stream idle timeout firing on custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateways despite server keep-alive pings arriving on the wire
- Fixed claude.ai connectors being falsely marked as needing authorization when the session token is invalid — they now show a `/login` hint instead
- Fixed tool errors not being displayed for tools no longer available locally, for example after an MCP server is removed
- Fixed `SendMessage` rejecting a long summary — it now truncates instead, so sends no longer fail on a character limit
- Fixed the spinner's effort label in a subagent's transcript view showing the session's effort level instead of the subagent's own `effort:` setting
- Fixed rare crashes when a file watcher hit a filesystem error or during file-watcher teardown
- Fixed screen readers re-reading the whole input line on every backspace in `--ax-screen-reader` mode — end-of-line deletions now echo just the deleted characters
- Fixed host model-selection keys not taking precedence over a stale on-disk `managed-settings.json` when `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST` is set
- Improved auto mode safety: messages sent to other agent sessions via `SendMessage` are now evaluated by the permission classifier before dispatch
- Improved the refusal when Claude tries to invoke a skill with `disable-model-invocation`: Claude is now told to ask you to run the skill instead of replicating its workflow
- Improved the `/diff` view, the Remote Control workspace diff, and file-edit diffs in Claude Code on the web sessions to use raw git blob content, ignoring workspace-configured diff drivers and textconv
- Changed Remote Control auto-start so repo-local settings (`.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`) can no longer turn it on (they can still turn it off); enable it at user scope via `/config`
- Removed ultraplan feature

### [`v2.1.221`](https://redirect.github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#21221)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/anthropics/claude-code/compare/v2.1.220...v2.1.221)

- \[VSCode] Added Focus view: a chat-menu toggle that hides tool activity behind an expandable per-turn summary with a live running-tool indicator, toggled with `Ctrl+Alt+F` or the "Claude Code: Toggle Focus view" command
- Added `mode: "mask"` for sandbox credential files on Linux and WSL — sandboxed commands read a sentinel copy (the whole file, or just the spans captured by an `extract` regex) while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on egress; on macOS file masking falls back to `deny`
- Added warnings to `claude plugin validate` when a marketplace or plugin name would be rejected by Claude Desktop's managed marketplace sync
- Added a `prompt-audit` subcommand to the `claude-api` skill for auditing prompts and tool descriptions for patterns written for older models
- Fixed a Bash tool permission-check bypass where zsh could execute hidden commands in `[[ ]]` regex conditionals; affected commands now prompt for permission
- Fixed PowerShell permission checks mishandling paths containing quote characters on Windows; such paths now prompt for approval
- Fixed the thinking toggle having no effect for the rest of a session that started with thinking off; disabling an MCP server mid-connect no longer silently reverts
- Fixed MCP servers from `--mcp-config` not being connected before the first turn in print mode (`-p`), which made the model emit tool calls as literal text
- Fixed @​-mentioned files being silently dropped when pressing Esc to retract a prompt and resubmitting it
- Fixed a crash when preparing API requests for SDK MCP tools named after built-in object properties such as `constructor`
- Fixed WebSearch failing with a 400 error at effort `xhigh`/`max` when thinking is disabled
- Fixed sandboxed large uploads failing with TLS errors through the sandbox proxy
- Fixed Team and Enterprise spend-limit message incorrectly blaming the org's monthly limit instead of your individual spend limit
- Fixed Bedrock authentication with AWS SSO named profiles failing in desktop-managed sessions on Windows machines that set a stray `HOME` environment variable
- Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN=0` not disabling interrupted-turn auto-resume; falsy values are now honored
- Fixed a rare wake-from-sleep race where two Claude Code processes could both refresh the same MCP connector or WIF OAuth token at once, forcing re-authentication
- Fixed renaming a session from Claude Code Desktop or claude.ai not updating the CLI's session name; session names from every rename surface are now sanitized
- Fixed plugin- and org-delivered skills named after terminal-only built-ins (e.g. `/help`, `/feedback`) being un-invocable in non-interactive sessions
- Fixed the "Plugins changed" notification lingering after plugins were reloaded instead of clearing
- Fixed Vim mode: the yank register now survives dialogs, history search, and the transcript view instead of being silently emptied
- Fixed Vim mode: undoing back to an empty prompt now arms the "press ← again" confirm before returning to the agent view
- Improved tool search on Google Vertex AI: re-enabled for Claude 4.5-generation and newer models
- Improved auto mode: permission checks for parallel tool calls are now cache-efficient, and switching modes while a check is pending reliably prompts instead of applying the stale result
- Reduced prompt-cache costs for auto-mode permission checks by reusing the cached conversation prefix across decisions
- Improved Stats panel to count cache tokens in its token totals, with a breakdown by input, output, cache read, and cache write
- Improved `/ultrareview` error messages when a repo shares no history with its base: a checkout with no branches is now refused up front with advice to create one, and refusal hints no longer suggest `git fetch --unshallow` on clones that are already complete
- Improved Windows startup: process creation times are now read via a native kernel32 call instead of spawning PowerShell, so endpoint security tools that gate `powershell.exe` no longer prompt
- Changed background sessions to commit and push to preserve work, open a draft PR only when the task calls for one, follow your CLAUDE.md git instructions, and always end by reporting where the work lives
- Changed `/plugin install` to refresh a stale marketplace catalog and retry before reporting a plugin not found
- Changed plugins installed from `/plugin` to activate immediately when safe, instead of always requiring `/reload-plugins`
- Changed plugins to accept `"."` as a `skills` path, and the root-level `SKILL.md` validation error now suggests using the plugin root
- Changed `/status` to show the session kind: `interactive`, or a background job that is `attached` or `unattended`
- Changed emoji autocomplete to accept common alternate shortcodes like `:thumbsup:`, `:thumbsdown:`, and `:love:`
- Changed sessions forked with `/fork` to create a new worktree of their own instead of working in the original session's checkout
- Changed Claude in Chrome to close the browser tabs it opens once it no longer needs them
- Changed fast mode to report on the stream when usage credits run out mid-session, instead of failing silently
- Changed Monitor: a watch that exits without producing any output now says so instead of reporting "stream ended"
- Changed the Gateway `model` field validation: non-string values are rejected with a 400 instead of being forwarded
- Removed the repeated "Permission mode changed while the auto-mode classifier call was queued" notice from approval prompts

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>anthropics/claude-code (@​anthropic-ai/claude-code)</summary>

### [`v2.1.224`](https://redirect.github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#21224)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/anthropics/claude-code/compare/v2.1.223...v2.1.224)

- Added self-hosted environments: `claude self-hosted-runner` turns your own machines or containers into a place Claude Code web, mobile, and desktop sessions can run, on Team and Enterprise plans
- Added `archive` plugin source: install plugins from a zip over HTTPS without git or npm, with optional SHA-256 pinning
- Added a cancel-and-confirm step when removing an unavailable paste changes a command's text
- Added `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX` env var for Bedrock to prefer a specific cross-region inference profile over the `AWS_REGION`-derived one
- Added `crossSessionInbound` and `dialogExpiry` settings: cross-session messages sent to a session running with bypassed permissions are held for your approval, and messages to other sessions auto-deliver
- Added sandbox credential-masking options: `extract` and `onExtractNoMatch` for structured env values, `decode: "jwt"` with `maskClaims` for JWT-aware masking, and `awsPairs`/`sigv4` for AWS SigV4 re-signing; these need `network.tlsTerminate` and are honored only from user, managed, or `--settings` settings
- Added cross-session `SendMessage`: Claude Code sessions can now message each other, on any of your machines, with `ListAgents` to discover them (macOS and Linux)
- Fixed long (>200 char) project paths resolving to another project's session directory under a shared sanitized prefix; session list, rename, fork, delete and `/resume` no longer cross projects
- Fixed `SendMessage` reporting "Message sent" when the write to a teammate's inbox had actually failed; failed deliveries are now reported as errors
- Fixed sandbox filesystem deny entries written with a trailing slash (e.g. `denyRead: "~/.aws/"`) being silently bypassable on Linux and macOS
- Fixed sandbox violation details never appearing in Bash tool results; Claude now sees which file or network access was denied and why
- Fixed MCP tools that connect mid-turn being deferred for tool search without their names announced to the model
- Fixed plugin install records being silently corrupted when the same plugin is installed in multiple projects
- Fixed recalled or restored paste content occasionally attaching wrong data or silently losing text when the paste had aged out or placeholder numbers collided
- Fixed copy-on-select on Wayland sometimes not reaching the clipboard; the two selection writes no longer race
- Fixed the feedback survey's transcript share silently failing on long sessions; a failed share now shows an error instead of a success message
- Fixed Remote Control auto-start intermittently failing with "Remote credentials fetch failed" on a cold start with a stale login token
- Fixed Remote Control and SDK clients showing a blank "(no content)" message after `/clear` and other output-less commands
- Fixed a Remote Control session recreated after its server session expired uploading prior local conversation history into the new session

### [`v1.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1110---2026-08-01)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/compare/v1.10.11...v1.11.0)

Security and correctness release. Repo-supplied worktree scripts now require explicit consent, path handling around the skills catalog and logs is hardened, `session send` tells the truth about delivery, restarted sessions can no longer resume the wrong conversation, and Ctrl+Q detach works on every session sharing a tmux socket.

##### Changed

- **BREAKING (exit codes): `agent-deck session send` now exits non-zero when a message reached the pane but was never confirmed submitted.** Previously `typed`, `typed_not_submitted`, `line_too_long`, `no_evidence` and `send_failed` all exited 0 and reported success, so automation that treated exit 0 as "delivered" could silently drop work at an agent's composer. Only `delivery: submitted` exits 0 now; every other delivery state exits 1 with `code: delivery_failed`. `--json` gains a machine-checkable `submitted` boolean so callers never have to know which delivery strings imply an accepted turn. Retry on `typed` / `typed_not_submitted`; treat `line_too_long` as non-retryable. ([#​1793](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1793), [#​1831](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1831))

##### Security

- **Worktree lifecycle scripts (`.agent-deck/worktree-setup.sh`, `worktree-destruction.sh`) now require explicit consent before running.** These scripts execute with the caller's full environment (SSH agent, tokens) whenever a worktree is created or removed — including from the remote worktree-mutation API, which has no terminal to confirm on. `[worktree] run_repo_scripts` (default `"prompt"`) gates execution per repo root + SHA-256 of the script's exact content, re-asking if the content changes; `"always"` restores the previous unconditional behavior and `"never"` blocks these scripts outright. A non-interactive caller under `"prompt"` fails closed with a remediation message instead of hanging or silently executing — approve ahead of time with `agent-deck worktree trust-scripts <path>`, or pass `--allow-repo-scripts` / set `AGENT_DECK_ALLOW_REPO_SCRIPTS=1` for a one-shot, non-persisted bypass (CI). The gate lives at the single choke point both scripts already funnel through (`RunWorktreeSetupAfterCreate`, and `RunWorktreeDestructionBeforeRemove` inside `RemoveWorktree`), so every caller — TUI, CLI, and the remote API — is covered without a per-call-site change. ([#​1810](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1810))
- **Skills-catalog path containment.** Managed skill targets are resolved through descriptor-pinned `os.Root` walks and re-verified by inode identity (`os.SameFile`), so a path component that changes between check and use is refused rather than followed. Symlinked ancestors, cross-filesystem violations, and mount points planted under a managed directory are refused; removal walks the tree itself instead of `RemoveAll`, unlinking symlinks without following them. The legitimate pool-attach pattern (final component is a symlink into the skills pool) is unchanged and pinned by a regression test. ([#​1809](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1809), [#​1811](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1811))
- **Log sanitizer barrier.** `logging.SanitizeValue` now rebuilds the string on every path; the old "nothing to escape" fast path returned its input unchanged, which made the function invisible to dataflow analysis. Non-UTF-8 input now becomes U+FFFD rather than surviving intact — deliberate, and pinned by a test. ([#​1809](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1809), [#​1812](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1812))
- **The Ctrl+Q detach binding no longer builds a shell command from tmux-supplied values.** The socket-wide binding is now a pure tmux-native `if-shell -F "#{m:...}" detach-client`, evaluated entirely inside tmux's format engine with no `/bin/sh` in the path. The same change is applied to `BindMouseStatusRightDetach`. ([#​1820](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1820))
- **Remote worktree creation is refused instead of half-performed.** `add --ssh <host> -w -b` no longer creates a local worktree for a remote session; it refuses with instructions. A bare positional path alongside `--ssh` now routes to `--remote-path` (and must be absolute) instead of being silently misused as a local project path. Thanks [@​kewtyboi](https://redirect.github.com/kewtyboi). ([#​1712](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1712))

##### Added

- **`[interval_hooks]` — run shell commands on a wall-clock cadence** while the TUI is running, independent of session activity: a periodic sync, a health probe, or a poll that dispatches work to sessions. Configured only in your own `~/.agent-deck/config.toml`. Thanks [@​jdidion](https://redirect.github.com/jdidion). ([#​1628](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1628))
- **Opt-in sparse-checkout inheritance for new worktrees.** `[worktree] sparse_checkout = "inherit"` captures the source worktree's mode and patterns and creates with `--no-checkout`, so a sparse monorepo never materializes the full tree first. ([#​1708](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1708), [#​1757](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1757))
- **Read-only `status --stale` candidate view.** Thanks [@​kewtyboi](https://redirect.github.com/kewtyboi) for the request. ([#​1704](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1704))

##### Fixed

- **A restarted session can no longer resume a different session's conversation.** agent-deck now proves the transcript it is about to resume belongs to that session before passing `--resume`, and declines to resume rather than attaching to someone else's conversation. This was observed live: a restarted child session picked up its parent conductor's transcript. ([#​1815](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1815), [#​1830](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1830))
- **Unknown `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`-inferred profiles warn and fall back** instead of silently selecting a wrong profile, and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is exported host-side so the value the session runs with matches the one agent-deck resolved. ([#​1790](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1790), [#​1791](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1791), [#​1822](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1822))
- **Usage-limit bounces are detected from the transcript, not pane text**, with a new usage-limit substate; pane-scraping false positives are gone. Thanks [@​AndreIntelas](https://redirect.github.com/AndreIntelas). ([#​1802](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1802), [#​1806](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1806))
- **Ctrl+Q detach is scoped per session, not per socket.** Key bindings live on the tmux *server*, and the old guard baked in whichever session started most recently — so on a shared socket every other session silently swallowed Ctrl+Q. Now matched against the invoking client's own session at keypress time. ([#​1808](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1808), [#​1820](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1820))
- **No more black screen on the first frame after detach**, and the redraw no longer costs O(visible rows). ([#​1753](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1753), [#​1774](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1774))
- **A start whose pane cannot reach its working directory is refused.** tmux silently starts the pane in `$HOME` when the directory is gone, so the agent would otherwise run against the wrong tree. ([#​1713](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1713), [#​1769](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1769))
- **The watchdog confirms liveness before restarting a session** — no more restarting a session that was merely quiet. ([#​1705](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1705), [#​1768](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1768))
- **Auth-hold sidecar plus a staleness check on death adoption**, so auth-dead sessions are held rather than flapped. ([#​1746](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1746), [#​1751](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1751))
- **Hermes session status reporting works** — env injection, turn-level hooks, and corrected turn-end mapping. Thanks [@​drmzperx](https://redirect.github.com/drmzperx). ([#​1807](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1807))
- **`-u` is passed on the remaining attach paths.** Thanks [@​Jonesxq](https://redirect.github.com/Jonesxq). ([#​1789](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1789))
- **UTF-8 is forced on the terminal-bridge tmux attach**, and **`inject_status_line = false` is honored** on the watcher/reconnect path. Thanks [@​hfreire](https://redirect.github.com/hfreire). ([#​1779](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1779), [#​1780](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1780))
- **Absolute `project_path` on every local session write path.** ([#​1766](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1766), [#​1770](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1770))
- **An explicit `launch -t` title is locked** against agent name sync. ([#​1715](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1715), [#​1750](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1750))
- **Detached sessions are born at the real terminal size.** ([#​1694](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1694), [#​1752](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1752))
- **Per-session ownership is proven before stopping a service-mode unit.** ([#​1754](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1754))
- **Detach/switch returns instantly at large fleet sizes** ([#​1764](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1764)), and frames are only rebuilt for width when they actually overflow ([#​1756](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1756)).
- **Releases carry SLSA build provenance again, and the Homebrew tap can no longer fail a release.** GoReleaser pushed the brew formula from inside `goreleaser release`, so when the tap token started returning `401 Bad credentials` the whole GoReleaser step failed and every step after it was skipped — including artifact attestation. v1.10.9, v1.10.10 and v1.10.11 therefore shipped with no provenance while `SECURITY.md` told users to run `gh attestation verify`. GoReleaser now only generates the formula (`brews.skip_upload`), provenance is signed *before* the release is published (so an unsigned release is never made visible), and the tap push is a separate best-effort step that runs afterwards and cannot fail the job. The tap push refuses to publish a formula whose version or SHA-256s do not match the verified release assets, and reports failures as a warning annotation plus a job summary instead of silently skipping. ([#​1760](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1760), [#​1763](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1763))

##### Documentation

- README session naming — title-lock, `sync_title`, groups. ([#​1703](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1703), [#​1823](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1823), [#​1828](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1828))
- Skill docs: `agent-deck try` scratch sessions ([#​1798](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1798)), fleet cross-reference and `session children` ([#​1796](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1796)), the session-manager vs process-supervisor boundary ([#​1797](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1797)), and the claude-subcommand flag-injection gotcha ([#​1801](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1801)) — all thanks [@​tarekrached](https://redirect.github.com/tarekrached).
- Substate guidance in the shared conductor CLAUDE.md template. ([#​1814](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1814))

##### Internal

- Stale-tmux reaper covers eval binaries and wider socket families, with a DRY\_RUN smoke test and a fixed launchd deployment. ([#​1749](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1749))
- Deflaked control-pipe, cgroup-decision and persistence-discovery tests ([#​1812](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1812)); made three `internal/session` tests host-independent on macOS ([#​1720](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/issues/1720), [#​1755](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1755)); `TestCanRestartCursor` no longer requires the cursor CLI — thanks [@​AndreIntelas](https://redirect.github.com/AndreIntelas) ([#​1805](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1805)); strengthened attach return guards — thanks [@​terminalchai](https://redirect.github.com/terminalchai) ([#​1787](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1787)).
- Dependency bumps. ([#​1785](https://redirect.github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck/pull/1785))

</details>

#### What's Changed

This release has massive changes, but most of them should hopefully not be visible: I completely overhauled lazygit's concurrency model, which was, let's say, less than robust; there were lots of data races, and we were just lucky that this didn't result in crashes or misbehavior more often. We now have a robust concurrency model with no known data races, and in fact we run our integration test suite on CI with the `-race` flag to prove that. The user visible part of this is that some operations run a little more smoothly now; for example, there used to be an ugly spinner freeze at the end of checking out a branch, which is now gone.

items.title: [FIX] eval_033 - diagnose BM25 side for chunk 596 (DTC revenue %)
items.body:
Closes #4

## Problem

`eval_033` ("What was Levi's DTC revenue as a percentage of total revenue in FY2025?", gt=596, acceptable=[603]) scored MISS. Chunk 596 was already enriched once in the residual-miss triage session (dense cosine 0.394 -> 0.619, dense rank 8) but never cracked the fused top-10.

## Why this change is needed

Every prior enrichment fix in this series only ever changed the Supabase `embedding` column (the dense leg) -- chunk 596's BM25 rank had never been checked. Measuring it directly this session revealed a genuine two-leg problem, and revealed a previously-unexplored lever: the *acceptable* chunk (603), never touched by any prior fix, had a much better BM25 rank and its own literal (but diluted) answer sentence.

## Changes made

- Added a targeted, content-accurate prefix for chunk 603 to `src/fix_misclassified_table_chunks.py`'s `ENRICHMENT_PREFIXES` map.
- Wrote the enriched embedding to Supabase (single targeted `UPDATE`, chunk 603 only).
- Regenerated `data/eval_results.json`.
- Updated `README.md`'s recall@10 partial/miss breakdown and by-type table.

## How to test

```bash
python src/eval_runner.py --fy-filter
pytest -v
```

## Validation performed

- **BM25 diagnosis** (new measurement, never done before): chunk 596's raw BM25 rank is 137/1,449 unfiltered, 59 within the FY-filtered candidate pool -- confirms a genuine two-leg problem that can't be fixed without touching `data/chunks_v2.json`'s raw text (explicitly out of scope). Chunk 603's raw BM25 rank is 34 unfiltered, 13 filtered -- much closer to the top-10 cutoff, and its own text literally ends with "DTC comprised 49% of total net revenues," diluted by ~550 preceding words about Europe/Asia/Beyond Yoga/Wholesale.
- **Local cosine pre-check**: chunk 603's cosine for its own question raised from 0.4744 (no prefix) to 0.6791 (specific prefix).
- **Cross-interference check**, before writing: checked the candidate prefix against 13 topically-adjacent FY2025-annual eval questions (eval_002/003/004/007/008/009/011/021/027/034/036/058/059). Where the projected similarity exceeded a neighbor's current gt/acc similarity, that chunk was protected by its own strong BM25 rank (same RRF-protects-strong-BM25-chunks pattern validated in the eval_053 fix) -- confirmed live afterward that none of the 13 lost their HIT/PARTIAL status, including `eval_027`'s chunk 528 from the immediately-prior PR.
- **Full regression**: `python src/eval_runner.py --fy-filter`, diffed directly against the committed baseline -- exactly one question changed, `eval_033: MISS -> PARTIAL`. Nothing else moved.
- `pytest -v`: 18 passed, 0 failed.

## Before and after

### Before
recall@10 76.7% (46/60 HIT), 7 partial, 7 miss.

### After
recall@10 unchanged at 76.7% (46/60 HIT) -- chunk 603 is `acceptable`, not `ground_truth`, so this moves MISS -> PARTIAL, not to HIT. 8 partial, 6 miss. Real (non-OOS-scorer-artifact) retrieval misses down to 1/60 (`eval_028`).

## Data or model impact

One Supabase `chunks` table row (id=603) had its `embedding` column updated. No change to chunk text, IDs, `data/chunks_v2.json`, `src/retrieve.py`, `schema.sql`, `app/`, or `frontend/`. No redeploy needed.

## Documentation impact

`README.md` recall@10 breakdown and by-type table updated. Full diagnosis (BM25 numbers, cross-interference check) recorded in `CONTEXT.md` (gitignored, not part of this PR).

## Known limitations

- Chunk 596 (the actual ground truth) remains outside the top-10 -- its BM25 rank can't be improved without touching `data/chunks_v2.json`'s raw chunk text, which is out of scope for this series of fixes. This question is now expected to plateau at PARTIAL, not HIT, under the current architecture.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests pass locally (`pytest -v`, 18/18)
- [ ] CI passes (no CI configured yet for this project)
- [x] README claims match the implementation
- [x] No secrets were committed
- [x] No unnecessary generated files were committed
- [x] Results are reproducible (re-ran `eval_runner.py` and direct `retrieve()` calls multiple times)

items.title: v0.8.3: pre-built embedded indices for mcp.Run (closes #10)
items.body:
## Summary

- **Pre-built embedded indices** ([ADR-024](docs/DECISIONS.md#adr-024-pre-built-embedded-indices-for-mcprun-v083)). SDK authors using \`mcp.Run\` can now pre-build their search index at \`go generate\` / build time and ship it inside their \`//go:embed\` corpus; \`mcp.Run\` auto-loads it at startup and skips the per-launch walk + chunk + embed pass.
- **Narrative**: \"v0.6.0 shipped embedded corpora; v0.8.3 makes their cold start fast.\" Closes [#10](https://github.com/townsendmerino/ken/issues/10).
- **Calibration discipline**: cold-start time, NOT recall. \`docs/BENCH.md\`'s hybrid-retrieval recall@10 numbers measure a different system and are unaffected.

## Three new surfaces

1. \`search.BuildAndSerializeIndex(fsys, opts) ([]byte, error)\` — library function.
2. \`search.LoadSerializedIndex(data, opts) (*Index, error)\` — library function. Typed errors (\`ErrCorrupt\` / \`ErrFormatVersion\` / \`ErrModeMismatch\` / \`ErrChunkerMismatch\` / \`ErrModelRequired\`) drive the lazy-fallback path.
3. \`ken build-index <corpus> -o <path>\` — CLI subcommand.

## Two mcp.Run integrations

- Convention-over-configuration auto-discovery from \`corpus/.ken/index.bin\`.
- \`Options.PrebuiltIndex []byte\` explicit override for non-conventional layouts.
- Lazy fallback to \`search.FromFSWithModel\` on any load failure (corrupt / version / mode / chunker mismatch) with a stderr warning naming the reason + suggesting \`ken build-index\` to refresh.

## Commits

1. \`feat: internal/search\` — serialize/deserialize primitives + binary format + walker \`.ken/\` prune. 11 unit tests covering full roundtrip BM25/Semantic/Hybrid + each typed error + forward-compat ken-version + determinism regression guard.
2. \`feat: cmd/ken\` — build-index subcommand. 5 subprocess tests (happy path, .ken/ auto-creation + double-build for walker-prune coverage, missing corpus, invalid mode, missing -o).
3. \`feat: mcp\` — pre-built index auto-discovery with lazy fallback. 6 integration tests covering each fallback / explicit-override scenario.
4. \`docs\` — ADR-024 + CHANGELOG + README + DESIGN.md updates.
5. \`docs\` — CHANGELOG housekeeping (v0.8.0 / v0.8.1 / v0.8.2 / v0.8.3 UNRELEASED labels dated) + mcp test rename.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI matrix green (postgres + sqlite + mysql + mariadb integration tests + 7 stdout-cleanliness variants + new serialization tests).
- [ ] gofmt / go vet / go build / go test all clean locally.
- [ ] FF merge to main as one update.
- [ ] Tag v0.8.3 from main → Release workflow builds 4-platform binaries.
- [ ] Draft GitHub Release notes covering the cold-start narrative (v0.6.0 → v0.8.3 arc closes the loop ADR-016 left open).

items.title: Make the accuracy claim reproducible: report metadata + mechanical scoring
items.body:
Implements **ТЗ №5** — make the accuracy claim reproducible. The claim couldn't be reproduced or diffed because no report recorded how it was produced. Fixed end to end.

## 1. Run metadata in the report ⚠️ breaking `--json-out` format

`--json-out` was a bare findings list. It's now an object:

```json
{
  "metadata": {
    "tool": "mem-audit",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "run_at": "2026-07-26T12:00:00+00:00",
    "user_id": "demo",
    "embedder": { "provider": "github", "model": "openai/text-embedding-3-small", "base_url": "https://models.github.ai/inference" },
    "judge": { "provider": "cerebras", "model": "gpt-oss-120b", "base_url": "https://api.cerebras.ai/v1" },
    "params": { "top_k": 5, "min_similarity": 0.3, "similarity_threshold": null, "max_retries": 5, "min_request_interval": 12.0, "page_size": 500 },
    "memories_scanned": 9,
    "candidate_pairs": 4,
    "judge_verdicts": { "DUPLICATE": 1, "CONTRADICTION": 1, "UPDATE": 1, "UNRELATED": 1, "skipped": 0 }
  },
  "findings": [
    { "type": "contradiction", "severity": "high", "memory_ids": ["m1", "m2"], "summary": "Contradiction: \"My name is LGY\" vs \"My name is LGS\"", "detail": "…", "suggested_action": "…" },
    { "type": "stale", "severity": "medium", "memory_ids": ["m3", "m4"], "summary": "Likely superseded: \"I live in Berlin\" -> \"I live in Madrid\"", "detail": "…", "suggested_action": "…" },
    { "type": "duplicate", "severity": "low", "memory_ids": ["m5", "m6"], "summary": "Duplicate: \"I enjoy playing chess…\" ~ \"I like playing chess…\"", "detail": "…", "suggested_action": "…" }
  ]
}
```

(Above is the actual offline-demo report, `detail`/`suggested_action` elided for width.)

- `version` comes from `importlib.metadata` (not hardcoded); it reads `0+unknown` on a bare source checkout, the real version once pip-installed.
- **`model` is the actual model used** (preset default or `--*-model` override); `base_url` records where it went. **No API keys anywhere** (asserted in tests).
- **Judge verdict distribution** over all four labels + `skipped` (rate-limit-exhausted pairs).
- Threaded via an optional `report_metadata` dict through `run_audit → find_contradictions`. Defaults `None`, so library callers/tests are unaffected and the bare-list partial format is preserved for them.
- **Incremental atomic write preserved**: with metadata, the partial file is the same `{metadata, findings}` object and stays valid JSON on interruption (test added, `KeyboardInterrupt` mid-run → object with the completed findings + live verdict tally).
- Console gains one dim line under the table: `embedder: … · judge: … · top-k: N`.

## 2. `analyze_confidence_test.py` scores itself

Was a checklist asking a human to match paraphrased summaries. Now mechanical:

- `confidence_test_seed.py` captures each Mem0 id at seed time and writes `confidence_ground_truth.json` (pair name → the two ids + expected type) next to the config.
- `analyze_confidence_test.py` matches findings to pairs **by memory id**, prints recall, precision, correct-type vs right-pair-wrong-type, false positives, misses, and the run metadata. `score(findings, pairs)` is a pure stdlib function.
- **`tests/test_confidence_analysis.py`** reconstructs the documented run as data and asserts `score` → **recall 7/7, precision 7/10**, correct-type 5, wrong-type 2, 3 FPs — so the headline number is reproducible in CI with no keys. (I could not run the live seed/analyze against a real store — no keys — so the end-to-end "on the current `confidence_report.json`" check is proven via this reconstruction, not a live run.)

## 3. README "Measured accuracy" rewritten

All three runs, numbers side by side (recall 7/7 every time; runs 2 & 3 byte-identical — same 76 candidate pairs, same 10 findings — so **not** LLM sampling noise; run 1 = 7 findings / 0 FPs vs 10 / 3 FPs later, with 2 update pairs typed CONTRADICTION). States plainly that the cause is not established and not recoverable (old reports stored no versions/params), lists what was ruled out, and gives the reader guidance: rely on recall, verify type and absence of extras by eye. No "generally stable"; no claim of LLM non-determinism.

## Commands run (clean venv: numpy rich click only — CI condition)

- `py_compile` over `mem_audit examples tests` → OK
- all **9** test files → pass (incl. `test_confidence_analysis`, `test_report` object form, `test_resilience` verdict/interrupt, `test_pipeline` metadata)
- `python examples/demo_offline.py` → OK
- `python examples/demo_offline.py --json-out r.json` → writes the `{metadata, findings}` object above; verified all 9 metadata keys present, `judge_verdicts` populated, **no `api_key` substring**
- `dev-scripts/analyze_confidence_test.py --report … --ground-truth …` on a synthetic report → prints recall/precision/metadata correctly
- README tariff grep → empty

## Not verified (no live keys)
A full audit against a real Mem0 store, and the live seed→run→analyze loop. The metadata plumbing and scorer are proven offline; I did not fabricate a live green run.

## Acceptance
- Clean-venv tests green (9 files); CI matrix 3.10/3.11/3.12.
- Offline demo works; `--json-out` in the demo yields a metadata file.
- Interrupted run leaves valid JSON (test).
- No API keys in the report (test).
- Accuracy section has all three runs' numbers.
- Full new report format shown above.

items.title: Round: source-count fix, CI, retraction checking, eval benchmark
items.body:
Improvements from the Fable repo review. Each is independently useful and tested.

## What's in here

**1. Source-count consistency + honest positioning** (`c82230a`)
- The tagline/pipeline diagram claimed **17 sources** while the sources table said 13. Ground truth in `pipeline/dfs.py::_PARALLEL_SOURCES` is **13 parallel sources** (+ optional YouTube, + 2 full-text enrichment layers). Made it consistent everywhere.
- Reframed the tagline from point-of-care ("Evidence at the Moment It Matters") to honest lit-review positioning ("Deep clinical evidence synthesis in minutes, not hours").
- Removed stale `harjass/medagent` clone URLs → `harjassgambhir/cram`.

**2. CI** (`92c2d73`)
- GitHub Actions runs the 160-test suite on push/PR via uv (Python 3.11 + 3.13), with a README badge.

**3. Retraction checking** (`0f63415`) — new `search/retraction.py`
- Before any paper is cited: PubMed `Retracted Publication` pub-type (free, already fetched) + non-PubMed DOIs checked against **Crossref `updated-by[].type == retraction`** (sourced from the Retraction Watch database, bounded + SQLite-cached).
- Flagged papers get a loud `⚠️ RETRACTED` marker, are downgraded to the lowest evidence grade, and the synthesis prompt is told never to rest a recommendation on them.
- Live-verified against the Wakefield MMR DOI (flagged) and a real NEJM RCT (clean). 5 new tests.

**4. Evaluation harness** (`c9800c4`, `866adbb`) — new `eval/`
- **Cochrane recall** vs [CLEF eHealth TAR 2018](https://github.com/CLEF-TAR/tar) gold (5 real reviews, 129 included studies). `search-only` mode (no LLM, reproducible) + `--full` mode (real pipeline).
- **Planted-error catch rate** — measures the verifier removing fabricated findings.
- **`eval/BENCHMARKS.md`**: a *versioned* running log — one row per commit, so improvements are validated on the same dataset, not just claimed. Includes methodology, what's independently replicable, known limitations, and a roadmap tying each planned change to the metric it should move.

### Baseline numbers
| Metric | Result |
|--------|-------:|
| Cochrane recall — full pipeline | 24.8% micro / 28.5% macro |
| Cochrane recall — search-only floor | 16.3% / 19.9% |
| Verifier catch rate / false-discard | 100% / 0% |

Honest floors (PMID-only matching; the full run was PubMed rate-limited without an `NCBI_API_KEY` — 117× HTTP 429). Surfacing that is itself a finding.

## Tests
171 passing (`uv run --extra dev pytest tests/`), network mocked.

## Not in this PR
Example reports (`examples/`) — competitor-researched, 10x-difficulty scenarios are designed; the actual runs + verified reports land in a follow-up.

items.body:
Tier T4 of `ROADMAP.enhancements.yaml` — trust, control, and legibility for the memory corpus. All seven GOV items, one id-prefixed commit each, full suite green after each. Tier status flipped to `done` (done_means met).

## What shipped

| Item | Commit | One-liner |
|---|---|---|
| GOV-1 | `a9120d2` | Contradiction inbox (`LinkGraph.all_typed_edges` + per-clone resolved ledger) + `/hippo:resolve` per-item verdict flow; SessionStart producer with no-double-nag against the T2 radar |
| GOV-2 | `5d33241` | `steer: pin` — bounded ×1.2 always-on lift in the base penalized loop; **corpus_format 2→3, SCHEMA_VERSION 4→5**; doctor "N pinned"; eval gates green |
| GOV-3 | `cdb3ea8` | Proposals carry evidence: `--check` prints the proposal-time HEAD baseline; `--rationale` fences the WHY into the body; consolidate skill renders a per-proposal rationale block |
| GOV-4 | `4e54690` | Floor & corpus change governance: per-clone watermark, `+N/−M` floor delta, whole-file-hash edit detection, surfaced-once; read-only `floor_change_peek` for the scorecard |
| GOV-5 | `d1c8482` | `/hippo:why` recall receipt: per-hit backend/edges/steer/salience; honest abstention reasons (untrusted → BM25-no-shared-token → dense near-miss vs floor); `--why` flag + skill + 4th MCP tool |
| GOV-7 | `26a86c0` | Author confidence tier (`draft\|verified\|authoritative`): **corpus_format 3→4, SCHEMA_VERSION 5→6**; renders at inject + recall_view; NEVER a ranking input (AST + behavioral pins) |
| GOV-6 | `97eb57f` | Trust scorecard (built LAST): one deterministic doctor rollup line + SEC-1-gated `hippo://scorecard` MCP resource; absent producers render as zero |

## The two clean-break pairs (as landed)

- **corpus_format 2→3 (GOV-2) → 3→4 (GOV-7)** — each a stamp-only additive migration (the GRA-4 precedent); init's seeding literal, README format history, and the per-bump pin test updated in lockstep each time.
- **SCHEMA_VERSION 4→5 (GOV-2) → 5→6 (GOV-7)** — each rides `refresh_index`'s metadata no-op compare extension (`steer`, then `confidence` — the 3rd and 4th fields needing the LIF-1/RET-5 starvation guard, both directions pinned).

## Premise corrections found against the live tree (T3 discipline)

- **GOV-5's abstention recipe quoted incommensurable numbers**: recall emits RRF-fused scores (~1/60 scale) while `_dense_floor` is a cosine (0.5–0.6). The shipped receipt probes `index.dense @ embed_query(query)` directly (entry rows only) — the true cosine vs the cosine floor. Recorded in-file as `implementation_correction`.
- GOV-2's roadmap note already carried the stale "3→4" bump numbers (T3 took 3→4); landed as 4→5/5→6 per the tier audit.

## Verification

- Suite: **1245 → 1324 passed** (12 deselected) — green after every one of the 7 commits.
- Eval gates (golden corpus, real bge-small-en-v1.5, dense+bm25): self_recall **0.98**, hard_recall **1.0**, mrr **0.9213**, p95 **28ms** — all pass; the corpus carries no `steer`/`confidence` keys so ranking before/after is byte-identical by construction (pinned by test).
- End-to-end smoke on a fresh scratch git repo (real model, real git): old-format corpus surfaces the doctor migration delta and rebuilds cleanly through BOTH schema breaks; pin lifts a borderline near-tie into top-k while a pinned-but-superseded memory stays below its successor (0.5×1.2 = 0.6× — pin never overrides a succession verdict); `/hippo:resolve` drains via both verdict classes (corpus edit + per-clone dismiss); `/hippo:why` explains a real hit, a dense near-miss (`0.558 < floor`), and the BM25-only no-shared-token branch; the scorecard aggregates real non-zero counts with absent producers as zeros.

No `plugin.json`/CHANGELOG bump (T1–T3 precedent: release mechanics stay separate). `requirements.txt` untouched — **no re-bootstrap needed**. MUTE (GOV-2's down-weight) and all read-side ranking beyond pin's bounded boost remain gated on the salience keystone (SIG-5/T7).

items.body:
## Prototype synthesis — Lead review of 11.3a, 11.3b, 7.4 (+ ADR-0016 and doc edits)

References #18, #19, #84 (all three prototypes merged: PRs #96, #97, #98).

This is the Lead's synthesis of the three completed prototypes, grounded in the foundation architecture (PRD, ARCHITECTURE, DATA_MODEL, ADRs 0001/0004/0008/0012/0013) — not a status report. Deliverable: `docs/verification/prototype-synthesis-11.3a-11.3b-7.4.md` (append-only; the three individual reports are untouched).

**Update (second commit):** the PR now also carries **ADR-0016** (`docs/adr/0016-mvp-vector-index-hnsw.md`) plus the doc edits the synthesis specified — DATA_MODEL §3.22 (names HNSW), §6 (materialized-tsvector implementation requirement), §3.21 (FTS index consistency), ARCHITECTURE §4.5 (search-flow note) and §12 (ffmpeg toolchain skew).

### Rulings

**Per-verdict:** All technical verdicts **CONFIRMED** —
- 11.3a: 5/5 (PROVEN against real Postgres 17.10 + pgvector 0.8.5).
- 11.3b: 5 mechanisms PROVEN + 2 INCONCLUSIVE confirmed as honest inconclusives (ADR-0012 threshold value; paraphrase recall by construction). The PROVEN-mechanism vs PROVEN-value distinction is preserved throughout — 11.3b proved the §6 plumbing, not any tuning value.
- 7.4: 8/8 + the disproven ffmpeg-vs-yt-dlp framing (a success of the prototype process).

**Overturned (1, process only):** 11.3a's "no ADR" call. The HNSW default meets the ADR bar — §3.22 explicitly left the index choice open, the choice is baked into a migration (hard to reverse), and it was a real measured trade-off. **ADR-0016 is included in this PR** ("MVP vector index is HNSW, not IVFFlat"), carrying the measured numbers and the honest scope limit (synthetic-embedder recall is internal-consistency only; ~2,000-video re-measurement owned by Task 12.8). 11.3b's "no ADR" is confirmed (no §6 change). ADR-0015 confirmed as-is.

### Key findings

- **447 ms hybrid latency is an implementation threat, not a design disproof.** Measured on a 12k-doc synthetic corpus dominated by per-query tsvector construction. Materialized tsvector + GIN is now a recorded Task 12.3 requirement (DATA_MODEL §6); the §6 formula itself is unchanged. Even unoptimized it fits Task 12.8's ≤2s P50 target.
- **ADR-0012 threshold deferral accepted**, but it has no landing task — a **new calibration issue is required** (being created separately by Neo; acceptance criteria in the synthesis §7/Q4).

## What this PR does

The measured write-up issue #19 asked for, mirroring [docshelf's demo](https://github.com/ignatenkofi/docshelf-mcp/blob/main/docs/demo.md) — plus the status flip it implies, and one real bug it flushed out.

- **`docs/demo.md`** — the numbers, all from tools or the ledger:
  - Case A: recall test **5/5**, INDEX 1,370 tok, query 1,765 tok (77.9% vs shelf dump, ~97% vs conversational source).
  - Today, via live `memshelf stats` on the 34-episode dogfood shelf: standing cost **8,638 tok** vs **1,924,800 tok** shelved mass → **222.8:1**.
  - The doctor's *first real findings* on the live shelf (below), the accidental-loss headline, the claimed-vs-realized methodology note, and a reproducible path (`stats`/`doctor` on any shelf + a scratch-shelf full loop).
- **Statuses**: README badges/paragraph → "M0 complete, M1 tools shipped"; ROADMAP M0 header → complete (2026-07-13 → 22) with exit criteria met; M0.md gains the "Case B and M0 close" results section (33 episodes, 1.91M → 5.7K tok, zero loss).
- **`fix(redact)`** (separate commit): the `env-secret` rule now skips already-redacted values — without the lookahead, doctor re-flagged every correctly-redacted `KEY=«redacted:env-secret»` as `secret-at-rest` forever, and `redact()` wasn't idempotent. +3 tests.

Closes #19

## Why

#19 was the last M1 doc deliverable, gated on Case B — which closed 2026-07-22 (verdict episode on the shelf). Running the day-old tools against the real shelf to *produce* the demo is the point of dogfood, and it delivered: `doctor` correctly returned `healthy: false` — two hand-era digests over the 120-word cap (the "agent honor" era measurably slipped), one secret-shaped string that inspection showed to be a deliberate dummy credential in a teaching recipe (reported by shape, judged by a human — no real secret, and none quoted in the demo), and an `index-bloat` warning (the M2 rollup motivation, observed in the wild). It also flushed out the redaction idempotence bug fixed here.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The dogfood shelf is private, so the demo can't offer a clone link like docshelf's; instead it leans on the reproducible path (`memshelf stats|doctor` against any shelf) and labels every number with its source and date.
